$comment: The Granular Delay's parameters, declared once.
Both the C++ dispatch and the TypeScript control table are generated from
this file, for the reason fx-01's manifest gives: a parity check between two
hand-maintained tables is a test that passes for a long time and then fails
once, after the drift has shipped.
Twenty-eight global controls and fourteen per tap, times eight taps, less
the ratio tap 1 cannot have because it is the reference the ratios multiply:
a hundred and thirty-nine parameters, which is what §7 specifies. Ids are
stable: globals from 1, tap k from 100 + 20k, so a ninth tap or a fifteenth
per-tap control could be added without renumbering anything a project has
automated. The per-tap blocks were produced by a script rather than copied,
which is why they agree with each other.
Several controls act only in a mode — Cross in Blend, Spacing and each Ratio
in Relative, Wear, Bias and Age on Tape, Stages and Clock whine on BBD, the
per-tap cutoff and Q with that tap's filter on. D1's render-delta base is
aware of that and puts the unit in the mode a row acts in before measuring
it, which is documented in granular_delay_delta_tests.cpp rather than
worked around by making every control do something in every mode.

params.name: Mix
params.note: Zero must null exactly, which §9 V1 measures at −140 dBFS.
params.apply: u.setMix(v * 0.01);

params.name: Topology
params.note: Selects the 2×2 routing matrix M of §1.2. Ping-pong is a matrix setting, not a special case, which is what V13 grades.
params.apply: u.setTopology(static_cast<delay::Topology>(static_cast<int>(v + 0.5)));

params.name: Cross
params.note: c in the Blend matrix; 50 % gives one shared feedback time for both sides. Acts in Blend only.
params.apply: u.setCross(v * 0.01);

params.name: Taps
params.note: Four by default: three or four playback heads is what the multi-head tape echoes had, §1.1.
params.apply: u.setTapCount(static_cast<int>(v + 0.5) + 1);

params.name: Sync
params.note: On, each tap and the feedback read take a division; off, they take milliseconds.
params.apply: u.setSync(v > 0.5);

params.name: Tap times
params.note: §5: absolute gives each tap its own time; relative makes taps 2–8 multiples of the first, by the spacing or by each tap’s own ratio.
params.apply: u.setTimeMode(static_cast<delay::TimeMode>(static_cast<int>(v + 0.5)));

params.name: Spacing
params.note: §5’s head-spacing presets. Acts in Relative mode, on taps whose ratio is Auto.
params.apply: u.setSpacing(static_cast<delay::Spacing>(static_cast<int>(v + 0.5)));

params.name: Feedback
params.note: Past 100 % is safe only because the loop saturator’s drive is floored there (§3.2); the runaway sits at a level rather than exploding.
params.apply: u.setFeedback(v * 0.01);

params.name: Feedback from
params.note: §3.2(c): the loop’s read is its own, not the sum of the taps. Longest tap is the documented variant.
params.apply: u.setFeedbackSource(static_cast<FeedbackSource>(static_cast<int>(v + 0.5)));

params.name: Feedback time
params.note: Used when Sync is off and the source is Dedicated.
params.apply: u.setFeedbackTapSeconds(v * 0.001);

params.name: Feedback division
params.note: Used when Sync is on and the source is Dedicated.
params.apply: u.setFeedbackDivision(static_cast<delay::Division>(static_cast<int>(v + 0.5)));

params.name: Feedback modifier
params.apply: u.setFeedbackModifier(static_cast<delay::Modifier>(static_cast<int>(v + 0.5)));

params.name: Loop LP
params.note: A one-pole, so its peak gain is unity and §3.2(a)’s condition holds without compensation.
params.apply: u.setLoopLowpass(v);

params.name: Loop HP
params.apply: u.setLoopHighpass(v);

params.name: Drive
params.note: 0–100 % onto a tanh drive of 1–12, and floored above 100 % feedback whatever this says.
params.apply: u.setDrive(1.0 + v * 0.11);

params.name: Character
params.note: Selects §6’s block. Tape by default, which is §9.1’s default case; Clean is the identity on both halves, which is what V2 depends on.
params.apply: u.setCharacter(static_cast<delay::Character>(static_cast<int>(v + 0.5)));

params.name: Time change
params.note: §6.2: Tape bends the pitch through the transport, Digital crossfades two heads over 20 ms, Instant jumps.
params.apply: u.setTimeChangeMode(static_cast<delay::TimeChangeMode>(static_cast<int>(v + 0.5)));

params.name: Smear
params.note: §4’s one control: grains per tap, spray, onset jitter and grain length together. Zero must null against a plain delay (V2).
params.apply: u.setSmear(v * 0.01);

params.name: Ducking
params.apply: u.setDucking(v * 0.01);

params.name: Width
params.apply: u.setWidth(v * 0.01);

params.name: Output trim
params.apply: u.setOutputTrimDb(v);

params.name: Quality
params.note: Defaults to High rather than the sheet’s Normal: the grain pool was sized against thirty-two streams per tap at full Smear, which Normal’s cap clips at exactly the setting §4 calls ordinary. Recorded in the ledger.
params.apply: u.setQuality(static_cast<delay::Quality>(static_cast<int>(v + 0.5)));

params.name: Bypass
params.note: A bypassed unit is still in circuit and still meters.
params.apply: u.setBypass(v > 0.5);

params.name: Wear
params.note: §6.1’s wow and flutter presets, graded by V9 in weighted RMS. Acts on Tape.
params.apply: u.setWear(static_cast<delay::Wear>(static_cast<int>(v + 0.5)));

params.name: Bias
params.note: Headroom, repeat level and top end all fall as it rises, §6.3 — which is what makes it a control distinct from Drive. Acts on Tape.
params.apply: u.setBias(v * 0.01);

params.name: Age
params.note: Older tape has lower bandwidth and a warmer top, §6.3. Acts on Tape.
params.apply: u.setAge(v * 0.01);

params.name: Stages
params.note: Sets the clock a delay time needs, and so how dark the line gets at long times (§6.4, V11). Acts on BBD.
params.apply: u.setBbdStages(static_cast<int>(v + 0.5));

params.name: Clock whine
params.note: Residual clock at f_clk, −78 dBFS by design (§6.4, §11). Under the −70 dB delta gate on purpose, so the gate is lowered for this row rather than the level raised.
params.apply: u.setClockWhine(v > 0.5);

params.name: Tap1 time
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(0); t.delaySeconds = v * 0.001; u.setTap(0, t); }

params.name: Tap1 division
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(0); t.division = static_cast<delay::Division>(static_cast<int>(v + 0.5)); u.setTap(0, t); }

params.name: Tap1 modifier
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(0); t.modifier = static_cast<delay::Modifier>(static_cast<int>(v + 0.5)); u.setTap(0, t); }

params.name: Tap1 level
params.note: −60 is −∞: the tap is silent, and its 4 ms fade is what stops that being a click.
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(0); t.level = v <= -59.5 ? 0.0 : std::pow(10.0, v / 20.0); u.setTap(0, t); }

params.name: Tap1 pan
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(0); t.pan = v * 0.01; u.setTap(0, t); }

params.name: Tap1 pitch
params.note: A pitched tap is read by a grain, because a plain delay cannot shift pitch; octaves, fourths and fifths are the musical set (§2).
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(0); t.pitchSemitones = v; u.setTap(0, t); }

params.name: Tap1 fine
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(0); t.fineCents = v; u.setTap(0, t); }

params.name: Tap1 filter
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(0); t.filter = static_cast<delay::TapFilter>(static_cast<int>(v + 0.5)); u.setTap(0, t); }

params.name: Tap1 cutoff
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(0); t.cutoffHz = v; u.setTap(0, t); }

params.name: Tap1 Q
params.note: Per tap only, not in the loop, so it carries no stability constraint (§7.2).
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(0); t.q = v; u.setTap(0, t); }

params.name: Tap1 reverse
params.note: Reverse is only coherent with a grain to reverse within, so it forces a grain of at least 30 ms (§2).
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(0); t.reverse = v > 0.5; u.setTap(0, t); }

params.name: Tap1 mute
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(0); t.muted = v > 0.5; u.setTap(0, t); }

params.name: Tap1 solo
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(0); t.solo = v > 0.5; u.setTap(0, t); }

params.name: Tap8 level
params.note: −60 is −∞: the tap is silent, and its 4 ms fade is what stops that being a click.
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(7); t.level = v <= -59.5 ? 0.0 : std::pow(10.0, v / 20.0); u.setTap(7, t); }

params.name: Tap8 pan
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(7); t.pan = v * 0.01; u.setTap(7, t); }

params.name: Tap8 pitch
params.note: A pitched tap is read by a grain, because a plain delay cannot shift pitch; octaves, fourths and fifths are the musical set (§2).
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(7); t.pitchSemitones = v; u.setTap(7, t); }

params.name: Tap8 fine
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(7); t.fineCents = v; u.setTap(7, t); }

params.name: Tap8 filter
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(7); t.filter = static_cast<delay::TapFilter>(static_cast<int>(v + 0.5)); u.setTap(7, t); }

params.name: Tap8 cutoff
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(7); t.cutoffHz = v; u.setTap(7, t); }

params.name: Tap8 Q
params.note: Per tap only, not in the loop, so it carries no stability constraint (§7.2).
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(7); t.q = v; u.setTap(7, t); }

params.name: Tap8 reverse
params.note: Reverse is only coherent with a grain to reverse within, so it forces a grain of at least 30 ms (§2).
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(7); t.reverse = v > 0.5; u.setTap(7, t); }

params.name: Tap8 mute
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(7); t.muted = v > 0.5; u.setTap(7, t); }

params.name: Tap8 solo
params.apply: { TapSettings t = u.tap(7); t.solo = v > 0.5; u.setTap(7, t); }
